title: 13 YEARS OF CHEAT CURLS: Was it worth it?
summary: NH reflects on 13 years of curling, most of it heavy daily cheat curls that built his best body part. He concludes cheat reps work and are safe when planned, but strict reps would have been as good; the real dangers are unplanned form degradation and misdirected tonnage, so use cheated reps only to extend a clean set.
claims: As a beginner obsessed with big biceps he naturally cheat curled for 5-6 years without knowing strict curls existed; he has curled for 13 years
Cheating is not morally wrong for bodybuilders; only effectiveness matters, and the strength-sport idea that a non-strict rep doesn't count is worthless
Cheat reps do work for hypertrophy: he did almost only cheat curls for nearly 10 years and biceps became his best body part
He did heavy cheat curls every single day, almost Bulgarian-style, and never got injured
In hindsight he would not repeat it: strict curls would likely have given the same results and are more consistent
A stupid method done long enough beats a smart method done once or twice; consistency rules
Cheating injuries come from unplanned cheating when ego makes form degrade mid-set, not from cheating willed from rep one
Use the same amount of cheat force from the first rep to the last; increasing the cheat across the set is the problem
He built his arms up from 10 inches and protects his biceps tendons carefully
The real problem with cheating is that it is harder to direct tonnage to the target muscle
Cheating means using momentum or leverage to bypass part of the range of motion; push presses and partial pull-ups are valid examples, not moral failures
His goal was a 100 lb cheat curl; he reached it and is quitting cheat curls because he no longer wants to chase the number
The cheating trap: more momentum lets the weight climb without more muscle fiber damage; cheating 10% and 50% give very different results
Only cheat if you decided to before the set; if you set out to do strict reps, keep them strict
His cheat barbell rows degraded into a hip hinge close to an RDL that trained hamstrings and glutes, not his upper back, until a subscriber pointed it out
Real ego lifting is when insecurity pushes the weight up despite knowing it won't build muscle; accusing others of ego lifting usually reveals insecurity
Best use: start the set strict and, once clean reps stop, add controlled cheated reps; 6 strict plus 3-4 cheated beats 6 strict
In his experience 10 cheated reps and 10 clean reps give very similar gains
Forced reps, momentum reps and controlled or assisted negatives all extend a set; arm isolations are very safe to cheat
Conclusion: stick mostly to clean lifting and stack cheat reps on top
exercises: same cheat force from rep 1; decide to cheat before the set
heavier load and extended sets; built his biceps
degraded into a hip hinge that stopped working the lats
momentum bypasses the bottom of the press
cut the part of the ROM you don't want
valid hypertrophy technique, not a 'wrong' rep
